nodes.label: IPO Mechanics & Pre-IPO Structuring
nodes.summary: The procedural stages of a Hong Kong IPO from sponsor engagement through to listing, including pre-IPO investments, HKEX vetting, SFC dual filing, placing mechanics, reverse takeovers, and PN18 clawback.

nodes.label: Sponsor Engagement and Due Diligence
nodes.summary: Every IPO applicant must appoint at least one sponsor (independent), which must conduct reasonable due diligence and submit a sponsor declaration.

nodes.label: MBL Rule 3A.02 — Requirement for Sponsors
nodes.summary: A new applicant must appoint a sponsor at least 2 months before the submission of the listing application.

nodes.label: MBL Rule 3A.10 — Sponsor Declaration
nodes.summary: The sponsor must submit a declaration confirming reasonable due diligence and compliance with the Listing Rules.

nodes.label: MBL Rule 2.03 — General Principles
nodes.summary: Seed anchor for general Listing Rule principles relevant to pre-IPO investments and fair market operation. Official source verification required.

nodes.label: HKEX Guidance Letter — Sponsor Due Diligence
nodes.summary: Guidance on the scope of sponsor due diligence, including business, legal, financial, and regulatory aspects.

nodes.label: A1 Filing and HKEX Vetting
nodes.summary: The listing application (A1 form) is submitted to HKEX, which reviews the application for completeness and compliance with the Listing Rules.

nodes.label: MBL Rule 9.03 — Formal Application
nodes.summary: The formal listing application is submitted in the prescribed form; HKEX may require additional information.

nodes.label: MBL Rule 9.11 — Vetting Process
nodes.summary: HKEX vets the listing application to ensure compliance with the Listing Rules and Companies Ordinance requirements.

nodes.label: SFC Dual Filing Regime
nodes.summary: Under the dual filing regime, a listing applicant files a copy of the prospectus with the SFC under s.38D of the Companies (WUMP) Ordinance, and the SFC has a 14-day objection period.

nodes.label: SFO s.105 — SFC Power to Object
nodes.summary: The SFC may object to a listing application within 14 days of receiving the prospectus.

nodes.label: Pre-IPO Investments and Special Rights
nodes.summary: Pre-IPO investments (PIPE or cornerstone) must comply with HKEX guidance. Special rights granted to pre-IPO investors (board seats, veto, information rights) must generally sunset upon or shortly after listing. HKEX Guidance Letter GL43-12.

nodes.label: HKEX Guidance Letter GL43-12 — Pre-IPO Investments
nodes.summary: Guidance on pre-IPO investments: special rights must sunset at or before listing; investments must be completed at least 28 days before A1 filing (or fully disclosed and subject to lock-up).

nodes.label: Reverse Takeovers and Backdoor Listings
nodes.summary: A reverse takeover (RTO) is treated as a new listing under MBL Rule 14.06B. HKEX examines the substance of the transaction; if a listing shell is acquired, the enlarged group must meet all listing requirements. Guidance Letter GL104-19.

nodes.label: MBL Rule 14.06B — Reverse Takeover Classification
nodes.summary: A reverse takeover (including a backdoor listing or shell acquisition) is classified as a very substantial acquisition and is treated as a new listing application.

nodes.label: HKEX Guidance Letter GL104-19 — Reverse Takeovers
nodes.summary: Guidance on RTO classification, including the three-stage test and factors indicating a shell transaction.

nodes.label: PN18 Clawback Mechanism
nodes.summary: Practice Note 18 to the MBL Rules sets out the clawback mechanism whereby institutional placing tranche shares are reallocated to the retail tranche if the retail tranche is heavily oversubscribed (typically 15x+).

nodes.label: MBL Practice Note 18 — Placing Tranche Clawback
nodes.summary: Sets out the clawback/retranchement mechanism for oversubscribed retail tranches. Official thresholds require verification.

nodes.label: Placing and Underwriting
nodes.summary: IPOs are typically conducted by way of placement to institutional and retail investors, governed by the Listing Rules and the Code of Conduct for Share Placings.

nodes.label: MBL Rule 10.02 — Underwriting Requirement
nodes.summary: A listing of equity securities must be fully underwritten unless otherwise agreed by the Exchange.

nodes.label: MBL Rule 10.03 — Placing of Securities
nodes.summary: Rules governing the marketing and allotment of securities in a placing, including the 25% public float requirement.

nodes.label: IPO Timeline and Listing Approval
nodes.summary: The IPO timeline spans sponsor engagement (T-4 months), A1 filing (T-2 months), HKEX vetting (4-6 weeks), SFC review (14 days), pricing, and listing (T+0).

nodes.label: Tranche Structure and Clawback (Detailed)
nodes.summary: Hong Kong IPOs are typically split into an Institutional Tranche (Placing) and a Retail Tranche (Hong Kong Public Offer), with default split of 90% Institutional / 10% Retail. Clawback Mechanism (Practice Note 18): retail increased to 30% at 15x oversubscription, 40% at 50x, 50% at 100x. Institutional tranche may be increased if retail undersubscribed.

nodes.label: Pre-IPO Investment Timing Restrictions
nodes.summary: Pre-IPO investments must be completed at least 28 clear days before filing the listing application (Form A1) or 180 clear days before trading commences (LR 2.03, 3.08). Special rights - veto rights, negative pledges, guaranteed rates of return, price resets on convertibles - are generally not allowed to survive post-IPO. Detailed disclosure in prospectus of investment terms, conversion prices, and dilution effects.

nodes.label: SEHK Listing Decisions LD59-1 to LD59-6 — Pre-IPO Investments
nodes.summary: SEHK guidance on pre-IPO investments, including acceptable and prohibited features. Covers timing restrictions, special rights, and disclosure requirements.

nodes.label: Reverse Takeovers — Bright-Line Test (Detailed)
nodes.summary: Bright-line test (LR 14.06(6)): A proposed acquisition is a reverse takeover if it constitutes a Very Substantial Acquisition (size ratios >=100%) AND there is a change in control (as defined in the Takeovers Code) within 24 months before or after the acquisition. Consequence: acquired business must satisfy all Chapter 8 listing requirements. The Exchange may aggregate a series of transactions over a period.

nodes.label: Sponsor Appointment and Due Diligence
nodes.summary: Step 1: Appoint sponsor, commence due diligence, prepare listing document draft.

nodes.label: A1 Filing
nodes.summary: Step 2: Submit A1 application form and draft listing document to HKEX.

nodes.label: HKEX Vetting and SFC Review
nodes.summary: Step 3: HKEX reviews the application, SFC dual filing review period begins.

nodes.label: Pricing and Allocation
nodes.summary: Step 4: Bookbuilding, pricing, allocation, and underwriting finalisation.

nodes.label: Listing and Commencement of Trading
nodes.summary: Step 5: Listing approval granted, trading commences on the Exchange.

nodes.label: Pre-IPO Restructuring
nodes.summary: Step 1: Corporate restructuring prior to IPO to establish the listing entity structure.

nodes.label: Financial Test Selection
nodes.summary: Step 2: Determine which financial test (profit, market cap/revenue, or market cap/revenue/cash flow) applies.

nodes.label: Track Record Check
nodes.summary: Step 3: Verify 3-year trading record period, management continuity, and ownership continuity.

nodes.label: Sponsor Appointment
nodes.summary: Step 4: Appoint sponsor at least 2 months before A1 filing; commence due diligence.

nodes.label: Filing Form A1
nodes.summary: Step 5: Submit A1 application form and draft listing document to HKEX.

nodes.label: SEHK Vetting
nodes.summary: Step 6: HKEX reviews the application for compliance with Listing Rules.

nodes.label: Prospectus Registration
nodes.summary: Step 7: Register prospectus with Companies Registry and file with SFC.

nodes.label: Offering Structure (Public Offer / Placing)
nodes.summary: Step 8: Structure the offering with retail tranche and institutional placing.

nodes.label: Pricing and Allocation
nodes.summary: Step 9: Bookbuilding, pricing, allocation, and underwriting finalisation.

nodes.label: Listing and Commencement of Trading
nodes.summary: Step 10: Listing approval granted, trading commences on the Exchange.
